newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge on industrial output data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge on industrial output data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures shrugged off their early weakness and shot up after the release of unexpectedly weak Japanese industrial output data, dealers said on Thursday.

Japan's industrial production in April fell a preliminary 0.4 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, against market forecasts of a rise of between 0.3 percent and 1.5 percent.
The lead December Euroyen contract rose to a high of 98.90 after trading as low as 98.76 earlier in the day on spillover weakness from Wednesday's sell-off.
The contract gave up some of its gains and stood at 98.85 at 0455 GMT against an IMM close at 98.79 on volume of 9,870 lots.
June JGBs were also off their highs of 123.60 and stood at 123.23 against a low of 122.32 and a previous close at 122.60.

The Japanese interest rate futures market came under pressure on Wednesday on rumours the industrial output data would be stronger than projected, triggering fears the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would have room to raise interest rates.

News the BOJ would release its quarterly business sentiment survey, or tankan, on June 25 instead of in early July as previously announced, also depressed the market although the BOJ said the earlier release did not indicate any change in its monetary policy.
